_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Physical Sciences P1 (Physics), November 2025 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. The guideline is
bilingual (English/Afrikaans); only the English is transcribed. memo_answer gives the guideline's
working and final answers (tick marks removed); diagrams, graphs and circuits are described in
brackets in the question text. Data sheets printed with the paper are not transcribed.
FORMAT: 150 marks, 3 hours, ten compulsory questions (Q1 multiple choice 20 marks).

subject: Physical Sciences

questions.context: QUESTION 1: MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUESTIONS. Various options are provided as answers to the following questions. Choose the answer and write only the letter (A-D) next to the question numbers (1.1 to 1.10) in your ANSWER BOOK, for example, 1.11 D.
questions.text: Vector B and vector –B are acting on the same point X. The angle between the two vectors is … A 180°. B 90°. C 0°. D 270°.
questions.memo_answer: A

questions.text: Two forces, F1 and F2, act on a point. If F1 and F2 act in the same direction, the maximum resultant has a magnitude of 13 N. If forces F1 and F2 act in opposite directions the magnitude of the minimum resultant force is 7 N. The magnitude of the two forces, in newton, is … A 10 and 5. B 16 and 10. C 3 and 10. D 8 and 5.
questions.memo_answer: C

questions.text: In the vector diagram below, the resultant (net) vector is ... [Diagram: three vectors F1, F2 and F3 drawn as the sides of a triangle.] A Zero. B F1. C F3. D F2.
questions.memo_answer: B

questions.text: A boy, who is standing in a lift, observes a 20 N mass piece suspended from a spring balance fixed to the roof of the lift. He sees that the reading on the spring balance is less than 20 N for a short interval. The CORRECT description for the motion of the lift during this short interval is that the lift is … A accelerating upwards B not moving C accelerating downwards D moving at a constant velocity
questions.memo_answer: C

questions.text: A car of mass m moving up a rough incline at a constant acceleration, a, under the influence of an applied force FA. The incline makes an angle θ with the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the surface and the wheels of the car is µk. The magnitude of the frictional force acting on the car, can be calculated as ... A FA - µkmg cos θ. B µkmg sin θ - FA. C µkmg sin θ. D µkmg cos θ.
questions.topic: Newton's laws: friction and inclined planes
questions.memo_answer: D

questions.text: The gravitational force which the earth exerts on the moon is … A directly proportional to the distance between their centers. B inversely proportional to the mass of the moon. C inversely proportional to the product of the mass of the moon and the mass of the earth. D inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
questions.memo_answer: D

questions.text: The centres of two identical metallic spheres, each carrying a charge Q, are a distance r apart. Which ONE of the following pairs of changes (made simultaneously) will double the electrostatic force that one charged sphere exerts on the other? (DISTANCE BETWEEN CENTRES OF SPHERES | MAGNITUDE OF CHARGES) A decrease the distance to r/2 | double the charges on both spheres; B decrease the distance to r/2 | reduce the charge on one sphere to Q/2; C decrease the distance to r/√2 | reduce the charges on both spheres to Q/2; D decrease the distance to r/√2 | double the charges on both spheres
questions.memo_answer: B

questions.text: Three small identical spheres, A, B and C is charged as shown in the diagram below. The distance between sphere B and C is r. +16 μC -4 μC +4 μC A B C r For sphere B to experience no resultant electrostatic force, the distance between A and B must be … A ¼ r. B ½ r. C 2 r. D 4 r.
questions.memo_answer: C

questions.text: The battery in the circuit diagram below has a potential difference of 12 V and negligible internal resistance. Two voltmeters, V1 and V2, are connected to the circuit, as shown in the diagram below. [Circuit: battery, ammeter A, a lamp, a switch and a second lamp in series; V1 is connected across the switch and V2 across the second lamp.] When the switch is open, the CORRECT readings on V1 and V2 will be as follows: V1 | V2: A 12 V | 12 V; B 0 V | 12 V; C 12 V | 0 V; D 0 V | 0 V.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer: C

questions.text: Which ONE of the following graphs best represents the relationship between the electrical power and the current in a given ohmic conductor? [Four graphs of P against I: A horizontal line; B straight line through the origin; C decreasing curve; D increasing curve (parabola) from the origin.]
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer: D

questions.context: QUESTION 2 (Start on a new page.) Three forces, F1, F2 and F3, NOT DRAWN TO SCALE, are applied to a crate of 25 kg as shown in the diagram below. [Diagram: F1 = 700 N in the first quadrant at 30° to the positive y-axis; F2 = 800 N in the fourth quadrant at 40° below the positive x-axis; F3 = 650 N along the negative x-axis.]
questions.text: Define the term vector.
questions.memo_answer: A physical quantity having both magnitude and direction.

questions.text: Magnitude and direction of the resultant of the three forces
questions.memo_answer:
x-components: F1x = 700 cos 60° = 350 N right; F2x = 800 cos 40° = 612,84 N right; F3 = 650 N left
Fx = 350 + 612,84 - 650 = 312,84 N right
y-components: F1y = 700 sin 60° = 606,22 N upward; F2y = 800 sin 40° = 514,23 N downward; F3y = 0 N
Fy = 606,22 - 514,23 = 91,99 N upward
Fnet² = Fx² + Fy² = (312,84)² + (91,99)²
Fnet = 326,08 N
tan θ = 91,99 / 312,84, θ = 16,39° (above the positive x-axis)
Direction = 73,7°
questions.memo_note: The guideline gives the direction as 73,7°, i.e. measured from the positive y-axis (90° - 16,39°); 16,39° above the positive x-axis describes the same direction.

questions.text: Magnitude of the gravitational force acting on the crate
Explain why the three forces will not form a closed vector diagram.
questions.memo_answer: The resultant force is not equal to zero.

questions.context: (Start on a new page.) Truck A, of mass 4 500 kg travels at a CONSTANT VELOCITY while towing bakkie B, of mass 1 250 kg. The engine of truck A produces a force of 11 270 N. The road surface exerts a frictional force of 8 820 N on truck A.
questions.text: Write down Newton’s Second Law of motion in words.
questions.topic: Newton's laws: friction and inclined planes
questions.memo_answer:
When a resultant/net force acts on an object, the object will accelerate in the direction of the force at an acceleration directly proportional to the force and inversely proportional to the mass of the object.
OR The net force acting on an object is equal to the rate of change of momentum.
questions.memo_note: The English text printed in the guideline for this question is Coulomb's law (a copy error); the Afrikaans text gives Newton's second law, which is transcribed here in English.

questions.text: Coefficient of kinetic friction for the road surface
questions.topic: Newton's laws: friction and inclined planes

questions.text: Frictional force exerted by the road on bakkie B
questions.topic: Newton's laws: friction and inclined planes
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 3.2.1.)
Bakkie: N = mg = (1 250)(9,8) = 12 250 N
fk = µkN = (0,2)(12 250) = 2 450 N

questions.text: Magnitude tension in the tow rope
questions.topic: Newton's laws: friction and inclined planes
questions.memo_answer:
On the truck: Fnet = F - fk - T
0 = 11 270 - 8 820 - T
T = 2 450 N
OR on the bakkie: Fnet = T - fk; 0 = T - 2 450; T = 2 450 N

questions.context: (Start on a new page.) A boy pulls a 10 kg block, that is attached to a 5 kg block by a light, inextensible string of negligible mass, with a force of 50 N at an angle of 30° with the horizontal as shown in the diagram below. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the surface and the 10 kg block is 0,18. The 5 kg block experiences a kinetic frictional force of 9 N. 50 N T 10 Kg 30° 5 Kg
questions.text: Define kinetic frictional force in words.
questions.memo_answer: The force that opposes the motion of a moving object relative to a surface.

questions.text: Draw a labelled free body diagram showing all the forces acting on the 10 kg block.
questions.memo_answer:
Free-body diagram of the 10 kg block (dot) with: normal force N (FN) upward; applied force F (FA) at 30° above the horizontal; tension T (FT) to the left; kinetic friction fk (Ff) to the left; weight w (Fg) downward.
NOTE: if arrows do not touch the dot deduct 1 mark; any additional force(s), deduct 1 mark.

questions.text: Normal force exerted on the 10 kg block
questions.memo_answer:
N = Fg - F sin θ
N = 10 x 9,8 - 50 sin 30°
N = 73 N

questions.text: Acceleration of the blocks
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 4.3.1.)
Fnet = ma
5 kg block: Fnet = T - fk: T - 9 = 5a ... (1)
10 kg block: Fnet = F cos θ - T - fk: 50 cos 30° - T - (0,18 x 73) = 10a ... (2)
a = 1,41 m·s⁻²

questions.text: How will the magnitude of the normal force calculated in QUESTION 4.3.1 be affected if the angle between the applied force and the horizontal decreases? Choose from INCREASES, DECREASES or REMAINS THE SAME. Explain the answer.
questions.memo_answer: Increases. The magnitude of the vertical component of the applied force will decrease (as the weight will remain constant) and hence an increase in the magnitude of the normal force.

questions.text: Use PHYSICS PRINCIPLES to explain why it is very dangerous when children are not secured in a child’s car seat when travelling in a car.
questions.memo_answer: According to Newton's first law, the child moves with the car at constant velocity. When the brakes are applied, the child continues in its state of motion at constant velocity (towards the windscreen, which can be fatal). When the child is secured, the belt exerts a net force in the opposite direction which stops the child.

questions.context: (Start on a new page.) A block of mass 8 kg is held at rest on a rough inclined plane which makes an angle of 20o with the horizontal by a force F that acts down the inclined plane. The block is connected by a light inextensible string which passes over a light frictionless pulley to another block of mass 6 kg. The 6 kg block hangs vertically at 2 m above the ground as shown in the diagram below. 6 kg 8 kg F 2 m 20o The coefficient of kinetic friction between the 8 kg block and the surface of the inclined plane is 0,25. Ignore the effects of air friction.
questions.text: State Newton’s first law in words.
questions.memo_answer: A body will remain in its state of rest or motion at constant velocity unless a non-zero resultant/net force acts on it.

questions.text: Draw a free-body diagram showing ALL the forces acting on the 6 kg block before motion.
questions.memo_answer: Free-body diagram of the 6 kg block: tension T upward; weight w (Fg) downward.

questions.text: The frictional force acting on the 8 kg block.
questions.memo_answer:
fk = µkN = µk mg cos θ
fk = (0,25)(8)(9,8) cos 20°
fk = 18,42 N

questions.text: Force F, that will keep the blocks at rest.
questions.memo_answer:
6 kg block: Fnet = Fg - T: 0 = 6 x 9,8 - T, T = 58,8 N
8 kg block: Fnet = T - F - fk - Fg∥: 0 = 58,8 - F - 18,42 - 8 x 9,8 sin 20°
F = 13,57 N

questions.text: The force F is now removed, and the blocks accelerate at 2,6 m.s-2. Calculate the speed with which the 6 kg block will strike the ground.
questions.memo_answer:
vf² = vi² + 2aΔy = 0² + 2(3,6)(2)
vf = 3,79 m·s⁻¹
questions.memo_note: The guideline substitutes a = 3,6 m·s⁻² although the question gives 2,6 m·s⁻²; with 2,6 m·s⁻² the speed is vf = √(2 x 2,6 x 2) = 3,22 m·s⁻¹.

questions.context: (Start on a new page.) A satellite of mass 500 kg orbits the earth as shown in the diagram below. The earth exerts a force of 250 N on the satellite. V r m = 500 kg M A learner argues that the earth exerts a bigger force on the satellite because it has a larger mass.
questions.text: Name and state the law that you can use to clarify the learner’s misconception.
questions.memo_answer:
Newton’s third law
When object A exerts a force on object B, object B SIMULTANEOUSLY exerts an oppositely directed force of equal magnitude on object A.

questions.text: Calculate the distance of the satellite above the surface of the earth.
questions.memo_answer:
F = G m1 m2 / d²
250 = (6,67 x 10⁻¹¹)(5,98 x 10²⁴)(500) / d²
d² = 7,98 x 10¹⁴, d = 2,82 x 10⁷ m
Distance above the earth's surface = 2,82 x 10⁷ - 6,38 x 10⁶ = 2,18 x 10⁷ m

questions.context: (Start on a new page.) Three identical point charges A, B and C, all of magnitude +100 μC, are equally spaced on a straight line in a vacuum. The charges are a distance of 3 cm from each other as shown in the diagram below.
questions.text: Write down Coulomb’s Law in words.
questions.memo_answer: The electrostatic force of attraction or repulsion between two charges is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

questions.text: Calculate the net electrostatic force experienced by point charge C due to charge A and B.
questions.memo_answer:
F = kQ1Q2 / d²
F(B on C) = (9 x 10⁹)(100 x 10⁻⁶)² / (0,03)² = 100 000 N right
F(A on C) = (9 x 10⁹)(100 x 10⁻⁶)² / (0,06)² = 25 000 N right
Fnet = FA + FB = 125 000 N right

questions.context: 7.3 A negative charge of -2 μC is positioned 10 cm from point P, as shown in the diagram below.
questions.text: Define electric field at point in words.
questions.memo_answer: Electric field at a point is the electrostatic force experienced per unit positive charge placed at that point.

questions.text: Draw an electric field pattern around with the -2 μC charge.
questions.memo_answer:
Radial field lines starting from the sphere, pointing inward towards the negative charge, not crossing each other.
Marking: correct field direction; lines starting from the sphere and not crossing each other.

questions.text: Calculate the electric field strength at point P.
questions.memo_answer:
E = kQ / r²
E = (9 x 10⁹)(2 x 10⁻⁶) / (0,1)²
E = 1,8 x 10⁶ N·C⁻¹ left (towards the charge)

questions.context: QUESTION 8 (Start on a new page.) The north pole of a magnet is pushed into a solenoid as shown in the diagram below. [Diagram: a bar magnet with its N pole moving into end A of a solenoid; a galvanometer is connected between the solenoid ends P and Q.]
questions.text: What is the polarity of the magnetic field of the solenoid at point A?
questions.topic: Electromagnetism: magnetic fields and Faraday's law
questions.memo_answer: North pole

questions.text: In which direction will the current in the galvanometer deflect? Write down TOWARDS P or TOWARDS Q.
questions.topic: Electromagnetism: magnetic fields and Faraday's law
questions.memo_answer: Towards Q

questions.context: 8.3 A coil with 350 turns has an area of 0,08 m2. It is held with its axis coinciding with the direction of a magnetic field of strength 0,6 T. In order to induce an emf in the coil, it is pulled out of the magnetic field in 0,25 seconds.
questions.text: State Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction.
questions.topic: Electromagnetism: magnetic fields and Faraday's law
questions.memo_answer: The magnitude of the induced emf across the end of a conductor is directly proportional to the rate of change in the magnetic flux linkage with the conductor.

questions.text: Mention TWO ways in which the magnitude of the induced emf can be increased.
questions.topic: Electromagnetism: magnetic fields and Faraday's law
questions.memo_answer: Any TWO: pull the coil out of the magnetic field faster; increase the number of turns on the coil; increase the area of the coil; use a stronger magnetic field.

questions.text: Magnetic flux linkage
questions.topic: Electromagnetism: magnetic fields and Faraday's law

questions.text: Magnitude of the induced emf

questions.context: (Start on a new page.) Learners investigate the relationship between current in a conductor and the potential differences across the ends of the conductor. The graph below is obtained from their investigation. GRAPH OF CURRENT VERSUS POTENTIAL DIFFERENCE I (A) 0,6 0,4 0,2 0 1,0 2,0 3,0 V(V)
questions.text: Is the conductor ohmic or non-ohmic? Explain the answer.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer: Ohmic conductor. The graph is a straight line from the origin. The current is directly proportional to the potential difference across the conductor.

questions.text: Dependant variable for this investigation
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer: Current

questions.text: Control variables for this investigation
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer: Any TWO: temperature; length of the conductor; thickness of the conductor. (Accept resistance.)

questions.context: 9.3 The learners intend to use the conductor to construct an electric heater that should be rated 150 W and draw a maximum current of 6 A.
questions.text: Calculate the gradient of the above graph.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer:
Gradient = ΔI / ΔV = (0,6 - 0,2) / (2,5 - 0,85)
Gradient = 0,24 (A·V⁻¹)

questions.text: Use a calculation to motivate whether this conductor is suitable to be used for this electric heater.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 9.3.1.)
R = 1 / gradient = 1 / 0,24 = 4,2 Ω
Required: P = I²R, 150 = 6²R, R = 4,2 Ω
The conductor is suitable: its resistance equals the resistance required.

questions.context: QUESTION 10 (Start on a new page.) The battery used in the circuit diagram below has an internal resistance of 0,6 Ω. [Circuit: battery (internal resistance 0,6 Ω) with voltmeter V across it, in series with a 5 Ω resistor and a parallel combination of a 10 Ω resistor and a branch of 17 Ω and 11 Ω resistors in series; switch S in the circuit.]
questions.text: Write down the term that is used to describe the underlined words.

questions.memo_answer: Emf / Emk OR Electromotive force

questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy

questions.text: Briefly explain the answer to QUESTION 10.4.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer:
Total resistance increases, the total current decreases, so the lost volts (Ir) decrease.
Vext = Ɛ - Vint, so the voltmeter reading increases.
